why: Step 06 did not refuse on plan quality -- the plan already cleared the battery and was kept_best. It refused because `end_noun()` in studio/episode_ref_official.py built a garbled end-noun clause: its FINITE guard (line 496) lists the verbs that must blank the "with X now in frame" arrival (turns, opens, closes, points, lifts, walks, strikes, falls, runs, keeps, pushes, pulls, takes, grips, thrusts, swings, reaches) but omits "leans". So when a shot's written `end` opens on a lean ("<Subject 1> leans ..."), end_noun() treats "<Subject 1> leans" as a noun phrase instead of blanking it, and the builder emits "with <Subject 1> leans now in frame" -- exactly what prompt_lint's P9 garbled-end-noun check (studio/prompt_lint.py:197-204) correctly refuses on T03 and T16. This is a deterministic code bug, not a content/plan defect: redoing plan (round 4) would burn another round and very likely reproduce the same lean-ended shot. The fix is one line -- add "leans" to the FINITE regex -- then redo step 06 so prompts regenerate with the correct (blank) arrival clause for those two takes.
finding_row: | F1 | step 06 prompts, T03 P9 + T16 P9 "garbled end noun" | 522s+206s+0.1s already spent on 3 plan rounds before this refusal; $0 so far | one-line regex fix in studio/episode_ref_official.py (add "leans" to FINITE) | needs fix + redo 06, not another plan round |
proposed_diff:
--- a/studio/episode_ref_official.py
+++ b/studio/episode_ref_official.py
@@ -494,7 +494,7 @@
 NP_END = re.compile(r"(?<![\w-])(stands?|fills?|filling|has|have|is|are|sits?|lies?|rests?|holds?|at|in|on|"
                     r"along|with|over|under|from|to|by|inside|seen|lit|drawn)(?![\w-])", re.I)
 FINITE = re.compile(r"\b(?:turns|opens|closes|points|lifts|walks|strikes|falls|runs|keeps|pushes|"
-                    r"pulls|takes|grips|thrusts|swings|reaches)\b", re.I)
+                    r"pulls|takes|grips|thrusts|swings|reaches|leans)\b", re.I)
 """A verb inside a cut end noun: "with the knuckly hand turns the key now in frame" (T9)."""
